pending_commit.commit_message: UPSTREAM: HID: intel_ish-hid: ISH Transport layer The ISH transport layer (ishtp) is a bi-directional protocol implemented on the top of PCI based inter processor communication layer. This layer offers: - Connection management - Flow control with the firmware - Multiple client sessions - Client message transfer - Client message reception - DMA for RX and TX for fast data transfer Refer to Documentation/hid/intel-ish-hid.txt for overview of the functionality implemented in this layer. UPSTREAM: HID: intel-ish-hid: request_irq failure On some platforms ISH interrupt is shared, which causes request_irq to fail. This requires IRQF_SHARED irq flag. But IRQF_NO_SUSPEND and IRQF_SHARED should not be used together, so removed IRQF_NO_SUSPEND flag. Anyway this driver doesn't require IRQF_NO_SUSPEND, as this interrupt is not required during "noirq" phases of suspending and resuming devices as well as during the time when nonboot CPUs are taken offline and brought back online. UPSTREAM: HID: intel-ish-hid: add printf attribute to print_log() Structure ishtp_device contains a logging function, print_log(), which formats some of its parameters using vsnprintf(). UPSTREAM: HID: intel_ish-hid: clarify locking in client code I was trying to understand this code while working on a warning fix and the locking made no sense: spin_lock_irqsave() is pointless when run inside of an interrupt handler or nested inside of another spin_lock_irq() or spin_lock_irqsave(). Here it turned out that the comment above the function is wrong, as both recv_ishtp_cl_msg_dma() and recv_ishtp_cl_msg() can in fact be called from a work queue rather than an ISR, so we do have to use the irqsave() version once. This fixes the comments accordingly, removes the misleading 'dev_flags' variable and modifies the inner spinlock to not use 'irqsave'. No functional change is intended, this is just for readability and it slightly simplifies the object code. lakitu: Fix race between mount-etc-overlay and systemd-tmpfiles Part of mount-etc-overlay involves unmounting /etc/machine-id and copying /run/machine-id to /etc/machine-id once /etc is properly configured. It's possible that other programs might have issues accessing /etc/machine-id during this time. systemd-tmpfiles-setup-dev.service accesses /etc/machine-id and has started to sometimes show errors that look like the following: Failed to replace specifiers: /var/log/journal/%m Failed to replace specifiers: /run/log/journal/%m Failed to replace specifiers: /var/log/journal/%m Failed to replace specifiers: /var/log/journal/%m/system.journal Failed to start Create Static Device Nodes in /dev. Let's avoid races on /etc/machine-id by ensuring 100% uptime on /etc/machine-id in mount-etc-overlay. We can do this by leaving the original /run/machine-id bind mount and pre-populating the overlayfs with the machine-id before mounting it.
